question: What does oracle performance measure when assessing program discovery?

results.text: Evaluation. We evaluate these two challenges separately. To assess program discovery, we measure oracle performance, defined as the test performance of the best program in the discovered pool, Q(A∗). This measures the quality of the best discovered solution, independent of our ability to select it.

When the metric is well correlated with test performance, much of the oracle performance is retained; when this alignment is weak, selection performance can degrade substantially. These results suggest that practical program selection is a major bottleneck for AgentSSL.

The gap between oracle and practical selection, however, highlights a central challenge for AgentSSL and SSL more broadly:identifying the best discovered program when validation feedback is weak. Table 2 reports practical selection regret when using the feedback metric for selection.

question: How much expert effort went into labeling the WildFin detection data, and how many boxes did it yield?

results.text: WildFin [17]WildFin is an in-the-wild fish video behavior classification dataset that is derived from a real-world ecology pipeline. The detection artifact from there dataset was obtained by ecologists hand-labeling bounding boxes for three species of interest (requiring over 320 hours of expert effort, yielding 21,116 expert-labeled boxes).

F.2 Experiment Details

For each dataset, we used three random seeds to randomly sample subsets of the full training sets (10% of all images for WildFin and 20% of all images for BuckTales). We execute the ecologist baseline program on all three of these random splits to produce the low-label domain expert baseline.

An ecologist implemented a program using YOLOv8, trained on this data, and used that detector for downstream tasks like cropping specific fish for behavior studies. We received their exact program and obtained our baseline results by executing them on our random subsets of their data.
